notes.title: ZKW-Forever early gameplay footage
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=RrDkjdyrOqw;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Wait.. What? :D[/h2]
Since the last post, we've been hard at work on a prototype (eight days of work!) for ZKW-Forever, just to see if we're crazy or if the jump to 3D would actually be worth it. 
Turns out.. It definitely is! (testing new features always took 15-30 minutes, because we got stuck playing the game instead of testing the feature >.> )


[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/7938712/9cd22238852e8516c3c734f90bf64099a56885c5.png[/img]

[h2]What now?[/h2]
First of all, I need to thank all of you. [b]You have no idea how much you helped us[/b] in the past couple of weeks with your comments and likes. It really comes to show how many passionate fans
are [i]still[/i] out there after all of these years! [i]THANK YOU[/i] (The last update for Reborn was in 2016!)

But the battle is not yet over.. [b]Keep the comments coming! Let's make this happen, together![/b]

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/7938712/9fd81a56ea251fee7504079ab1370b49cb14d51c.png[/img]

[h2]Why do we need another ZKW again..?[/h2]
I've always had big dreams about what I wanted to do with ZKW. Unfortunately, I was always very limited with what I could do by either my skills, or resources. This lead to ZKW being a 2D side-scroller game, which limited what I could do even more. Don't get me wrong, I adore Reborn for what it is, and I'm still proud of what I was able to accomplish with what I had back then. 
[i]But I always felt like there should be.. more.. [/i]


[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/7938712/d9b6d8fe2a71b7052eaee69a25f1bd3b64405cc0.png[/img]

[h2]Any new features?[/h2]
Yes! Here's a short list of new stuff that's been planned:
[list]
[*] Split-screen multiplayer!
[*] Faster combat!
[*] More complex levels! (thanks to switching cameras to FPS / 3D)
[*] New weapons and zombies!
[*] More unlockables! (Perks, Overkills, weapons..)
[*] Weekly and monthly online events! (finally, become the Zombie Killer of the Week!)
[*] Social events!
[/list]


[h3]On top of all that, pretty much everything you loved in Reborn is already planned to make a comeback in Forever![/h3]
[list]
[*] Round based zombies
[*] Online multiplayer
[*] Player customization
[*] Bots [i](bless those idiots)[/i]
[*] Bosses
[*] Challenge / Highscore mode
[*] A wide variety of zombies
[*] Multiple levels to choose from
[*] Skill systems
[*] Crafting
[*] OverKills
[*] Powerups
[*] Wacky random machines
[*] Upgradeable weapons
[*] Daily missions
[*] Perks
[*] And more!
[/list]

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/7938712/9908973a38b51ceb345c5191cee4eb299c00e598.png[/img]
[h2]Ok cool, but what about..[/h2]
Did I miss a feature you'd love to see in the new game? Let us know in the comments below!


Once again, thank you all for your continued support after all these years. It's just mindblowing to me to see how many of you are still here :')
[i]PS. To that one guy who complimented on my mustache.
Thanks![/i]

notes.title: Zombie Kill of the Week: Forever announced!
notes.content:
[h2]This is going to be a bit of a weird one, but I'm going to need the help of all of you.[/h2]

Still Running is in a bit of a rough spot, as are many more developers at this day and age.
The market is tough, and publishers are being more careful than ever.

After years of working on Morbid, I've really wanted to get back to my roots.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/7938712/267463cd8ee425ca5d029811e8dae7c31fb120f4.png[/img]

[h2]I want to reboot ZKW, with Zombie Kill of the Week - Forever[/h2]

But unfortunately, just an idea, pitch, design, prototype.. those aren't enough anymore.
[b]We need to be able to show to our publisher, that there's demand for another ZKW title.[/b]

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/7938712/49ff13ea6a5b12f7ec93cbe3ac425b0e9d7f5bf0.png[/img]

So I'm asking you, please comment / react / anything, if you'd like to see ZKW dug up from the grave with yet another game in the franchise.

My plan was originally to shadow-drop another ZKW when Still Running turns 10 years old in just a couple of months. But we're not going to survive that long.

So now's your time to show us, and the publisher, that you want it.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/7938712/6cd11c2d0af698be54bb913066def3eb2cd6eb71.png[/img]

Enjoy the couple of concepts I uploaded here, and if you want to see my face and my face talking about this same subject, feel free to check out this video from YouTube:

notes.title: End of an era
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/7938712/23a9e843d624c41e29986fb680b21f8f672f9a5b.jpg[/img]

[h1]ZKW-Reborn will be removed from the Play Store on June 5th.[/h1]

Google has been looking for apps that use older development tools within them, that may cause the app to have some sort of an security issue, since 2016.

Until now, Google has only blocked these apps from being updated (if they haven't updated the development tools that had the security issue in the first place) but now, Google is actually starting to remove any apps from it's Play Store that still have the outdated development tools in use. Including ZKW-Reborn.

[h1]And you're saying you're too lazy to click that "update" button?[/h1]
Unfortunately, there is basically nothing I can do to stop this from happening. The only thing that would prevent this, is to update ZKW in the Play Store, but that is quite simply too late for that. Since the game was made with a really old version of GameMaker Studio 1, bringing the game up to Studio 1.4, and then Studio 2 would be a-LOT of hassle in itself, but it'd also require a ton of other development tools to be updated, as well as (obviously) making sure everything worked as they should.
Even if I did this, I would also need to update every other platform the game is on (iOS, Windows, Mac) since it is a cross-platform multiplayer afterall, and updating only one version would cause serious issues within the game.
And, that's not even all there is. The server is also made in GameMaker, meaning that I'd need to update that as well.
All in all, all this would take me something like 6 months to make, which at this point is too late, since the removal will be happening in less than a month.

[h1]So, what happens next?[/h1]
As far as I know, anyone who has previously installed ZKW-Reborn on their Android device, will still be able to re-download it, activate any in-app-purchases (such as Full Version) and play the game to it's fullest. With the exception of not being able to purchase any more ZKW-Points or anything else with real money within the game.

With that said, I will still keep the multiplayer servers up and running. Android version is still bringing in more money, than Steam and iOS combined, so I'm not too sure how long I'm going to be able to keep the servers up. But I'll try my best to keep them running as long as there are players around.

[h1]Me is anger !!1![/h1]
I'm sure I'm going to piss a-lot of you guys off, but trust me. I'm pissed as well. ZKW-Reborn was the first game I ever released with Still Running, and Android was the first platform I ever released a game to. ZKW-Reborn kept me alive for the longest time, and the community of the game has been super passionate, and I appreciate that.
ZKW-Reborn wouldn't exist without you guys.
Still Running wouldn't exist without you guys.

[b]Thank you.[/b]
Hail ZKW-Reborn. Have fun while it still last's. Let's make this final month of ZKW-Reborn the biggest in years!

The Deep Ones—as we now know them—were born alongside our own consciousness.

notes.title: Zombie Kill of the Week - Aftermath
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/7938712/5f5e3e00e47d92abf031925d3b730c5cc9369711.gif[/img]

[h1]ZKW-Aftermath will be the fourth installment in the ZKW game series. Yes. There will be another ZKW.[/h1]

There isn't much I can tell you about this project just yet, but I'll tell you a story.

When we started working on The Walking Vegetables, we knew we'd at one point make another sequel for ZKW. We wanted to keep this as a secret, and tell you guys about it after TWV was done, and we were happy with the game.
Unfortunately, TWV wasn't as successful as we'd hope for. We can't work on games for full time anymore, which means that there will have to be compromises made.

We will still be finishing The Walking Vegetables, as we have tons and tons of cool ideas on what to do with that game. Yes, there will be a mobile version of the game within the next few months, so that more of you could give the game a chance, and maybe support us by purchasing the full version. There will be online multiplayer as well, and much more.

After all this, we'll start working on ZKW-Aftermath. With that said, we're basically already working on that game, as we're already planning on where to go with the new ZKW installment.

[h1]What will be different on Aftermath VS Reborn?[/h1]
Everything you know and love in ZKW-Reborn will make a return. And there will be a ton of new features (a campaign mode, just to name one) and improvements. But there will be one HUGE difference with the new game:

This time around, I won't be making the game within the old ZKW engine, that I used with every other ZKW installment. Why? Because it sucks. Hard.

Instead, I'll be using the engine that was made for TWV. Because of this, the way the game is displayed will change from side scrolling game, to a "2.5D top-down view" such as in TWV. With this change however, we're able to make MUCH more complicated levels, with MUCH more detail in them AND! Get this! AND! I can actually make an AI, that WILL find the player! Wether it'll be the dumb bots who try to revive dead player, or dumber zombies, they. will. find. you.

There are some huge reasons why we're doing this. First of all, I used over six months building the engine alone. I made everything very flexible, and easy to add new stuff in mind. In ZKW-Reborn, it took me four hours to add a new weapon. In TWV however, it only takes a couple of minutes.
So basically, with this we're able to cut down some serious development time, and just concentrate on making the actual game, instead of working six months on the engine.
We would also had been changing the perspective of the game anyways, so it just makes sense.
Plus, since we'll start working on the actual game after TWV is done, it'll mean that we'll basically have a working online multiplayer on launch.

[h1]Random blabbering about stuff[/h1]
I'm very proud of the engine I made for TWV, and I do not want to throw it all away for nothing. Do not worry though. Recycling the engine does NOT mean that the game will feel like just a re-skinned TWV. It won't. The gameplay will be the same as on every other installment of ZKW, just turned up to 11.

Anyway, we already have tons of very cool and interesting ideas for ZKW-Aftermath, and since we now actually have a whole team working on a ZKW game (instead of just me) I'm sure we can be able to make something incredible.

Right, I think that's all for now.
I'm glad to see so many of you old ZKW fans still around here, and I hope we can bring you the sequel you all deserve. Actually, I know we can. ZKW-Aftermath will be an amazing game.
Thank you for sticking around all these years. Now I feel like I can get back to working with ZKW again. I feel like I have something more to give. I'm very excited about ZKW-Aftermath, and I hope you guys are too. (but seriously. In case you haven't, CHECK OUT TWV! Seriously! Give it a chance. You won't be disappointed)

https://www.facebook.com/StillrunningGame/

https://twitter.com/StillRunningZKW

notes.title: I'm back!
notes.content:
[img]https://media.tenor.com/images/ba6623de3084c7752abe0d2323ddca28/tenor.gif[/img]

[h1]Been a YEAR! Where have you been!?[/h1]
Yeah, about that. I sort of may have lied about being back. I mean, I'm back for sure, but maybe not in the way you guys were expecting.

First things first, this announcement is actually not about ZKW-Reborn.
I have something else to show you guys..

[img]https://scontent-arn2-1.xx.fbcdn.net/v/t31.0-8/18699585_1321294287989493_5524736218514589925_o.jpg?oh=817f332d86faeae2515bcd85ba9764dc&oe=5A52DD56[/img]

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/704840/The_Walking_Vegetables/] The Walking Vegetables - Steam page [/url] 

[i]It's vegetables. Yes. You read it right. Moving on?[/i]

[h1]Does this mean ZKW-Reborn is not supported anymore?[/h1]
Nnno. It does not mean that. In case you haven't noticed, the profile and multiplayer servers are still running [i](see what I did there) [/i] and I'm still around, answering your questions and helping people out. So no, I will still support ZKW-Reborn. Afterall, I worked on that game for 6 years. I'm not just going to throw all that away.

What this DOES mean however, is that (again, if you've been living under a rock) I do not have any future plans for ZKW-Reborn. The game is finished in my eyes, and even though I had some big plans for future updates, I was not able to complete them, as I've been getting better and better with coding during the development of ZKW, and as it stands now, some of the code in the game is outright awful. If I were to make [b]any[/b] big changes into the game, that would basically mean that I'd have to re-write the whole game from scratch. And that's not a really easy task to accomplish.

[h1]Ha! You're still talking about ZKW![/h1]
Ah yes, shall we move on now?


[img]https://pbs.twimg.com/media/DHbqJ5cXsAAdjSf.jpg[/img]

[h1]The Walking Vegetables[/h1]
Is a game I've been working on with a friend of mine for the last year. It was supposed to be a small brainfart of an game, but then again, that's exactly how ZKW started it's life. Except, with one crucial difference.. Actually, two.

[b]1.[/b] First of all, I'm not alone this time. Just think how good The Walking Vegetables can be, if I was able to make ZKW on my own basically? Now, I have two more people working on The Walking Vegetables full time! More on that later.. Stick with us..

[b]2.[/b] Me. Yes, I actually did just do that, I listed myself here.
My coding skills have drastically improved from the times of ZKW. Even from ZKW-Reborn. I'm able to do things I couldn't even imagine doing when I worked on ZKW. Alright, I think that's enough for me to brag about myself.. 


[h1]Ok ok.. It's not ZKW, but go on..[/h1]
Thank you!

So as I was saying, The Walking Vegetables started it's life as a brainfart. I wanted to do something else than ZKW, make something fresh for a while. I called a friend of mine, who I actually have worked with maaany years back. He told me he had this idea, this idiotically chaotic idea. Vegetable shooting. Shooting.. Vegetables. Because logic.
It was so stupid idea, of course we had no choice but to make it happen!

We started to work on The Walking Vegetables as a small free time project kind of a deal. Days went by, and I was asked to visit this local game event.
I rushed into one of those supermarkets, and got myself this shi..y clone xbox one controller, and made the game to work on a gamepad for the event.
I went there, and showed The Walking Vegetables.
And you know what?
People actually liked it. I mean, for god sake, one guy played it for over an hour and asked me where can he buy the game?
I didn't know what was going on. But later that day, I called my friend. Told him, that we had something in our hands.. Something much, much bigger, than we ever imagined (still talking about the game here guys. Stay in topic)

Thankfully, we realized that, and started to act on it.
Months went by, and we had tons of fun. Still Running team also grew to three people during the development. We got ourselves an in-house composer, who started to work on those radical tunes that can be heard in The Walking Vegetables.

[h1]I don't care, just show us something to look at[/h1]
Oh yeah. Sorry, I have this habit of turning everything into a wall of text.

[img]http://files.1337upload.net/screenshot_logo__248_-435747.png[/img]

The Walking Vegetables has a live Steam page that you guys should be checking out!
From there one can find even more of me blabbering about the game, and check out the radical gameplay trailer, and an actual animation that was made for TWV to tell everyone the deeeeep storyline behind TWV.


[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/704840/The_Walking_Vegetables/] The Walking Vegetables - Steam page [/url] 

And again, thank you all for sticking around! I've said this many times, and will continue to do so, but you guys are the reason why I'm making games. Stay awesome people!

[img]https://pbs.twimg.com/media/DHbqJ5cXsAAdjSf.jpg[/img]

[b]1.[/b] First of all, I'm not alone this time. Just think how good The Walking Vegetables can be, if I was able to make ZKW on my own basically? Now, I have two more people working on The Walking Vegetables full time! More on that later.. Stick with us..

[b]2.[/b] Me. Yes, I actually did just do that, I listed myself here.

I called a friend of mine, who I actually have worked with maaany years back. He told me he had this idea, this idiotically chaotic idea. Vegetable shooting. Shooting.. Vegetables. Because logic.
It was so stupid idea, of course we had no choice but to make it happen!

We started to work on The Walking Vegetables as a small free time project kind of a deal. Days went by, and I was asked to visit this local game event.
I rushed into one of those supermarkets, and got myself this shi..y clone xbox one controller, and made the game to work on a gamepad for the event.
I went there, and showed The Walking Vegetables.
And you know what?
People actually liked it. I mean, for god sake, one guy played it for over an hour and asked me where can he buy the game?
I didn't know what was going on. But later that day, I called my friend. Told him, that we had something in our hands.. Something much, much bigger, than we ever imagined (still talking about the game here guys. Stay in topic)

Thankfully, we realized that, and started to act on it.
Months went by, and we had tons of fun. Still Running team also grew to three people during the development. We got ourselves an in-house composer, who started to work on those radical tunes that can be heard in The Walking Vegetables.

Oh yeah. Sorry, I have this habit of turning everything into a wall of text.

[img]http://files.1337upload.net/screenshot_logo__248_-435747.png[/img]

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/704840/The_Walking_Vegetables/] The Walking Vegetables - Steam page [/url]

notes.title: [!!] Black screen on startup?
notes.content:
[img]https://media.tenor.com/images/f44d99fbbe49d9de2836418cf2046036/tenor.gif[/img]

[h1]In case ZKW-Reborn launches at black screen..[/h1]
and you have updated your [b]Windows 10[/b] to the [b]creators update[/b], then there's a very high chance that ZKW-Reborn (among some other games) can go into a plain black screen on startup, even though the game is still running (no pun intended) in the background, and you can hear the music.

[h1]How to fix this?[/h1]
The issue can be fixed in most cases, thankfully.
You need to go to :

[b]C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Zombie Kill of the Week - Reborn[/b]

and then find the [b]options.ini[/b] file. Open this with a regular text editor app, and change the [WINDOWS] portion of the ini file as following:

[b]
[Windows]
CreateTexturesOnDemand=1
AlternateSyncMethod=1
VertexBufferMethod=1
SleepMargin=10
[/b]

I know this is a stupid workaround, but as it stands, there's really nothing I can do to fix this issue. It's very frustrating for me as a developer, and I truly hope you will understand that this is not directly the game's fault.


[h1]Old stuff[/h1]
[strike]As for right now, I, unfortunately, don't know. I have only now realized the link between the Creators update, and this black screen issue. I'm trying to look into it, and in case I find a solution (or if any of you know how to get around this) I will update this blog post to give the solution to you[strike]

[h1]So what. We just supposed to sit here, an cry?[/h1]
If that's something you want to do, I'm not going to stop you from doing so.
But if not, no. You can still play the game on windowed mode just regularly. Alt+Tab trick doesn't seem to be working for most, but it's something you should try anyways.
For now, all we can do, is to sit tight, and hope that Microsoft will get this issue fixed. So keep your Windows up to date, in case the miracle happens!

ps: Here's some more info about the issue:

http://answers.ea.com/t5/Technical-Issues/W10-Creators-Update-broke-fullscreen-mode/td-p/5983995

notes.title: Campaign mode for ZKW?
notes.content:
[img]https://scontent-arn2-1.xx.fbcdn.net/v/l/t1.0-9/13177732_973672126085046_1575411422604859055_n.jpg?oh=616da7abb6213dbb20fc9ffe0b210f4f&oe=57E6F38E[/img]

Here's a picture of a doge.
Now that I have your attention, let me ask you something.
ZKW, and campaign mode.
Yay, or nay?

[h1]Let me explain a bit further.[/h1]
I'm sure all of you already know, that after the first few hundred rounds, ZKW tends to get boring. I've tried to come up with multiple ideas that would make the game more interesting, even on the later rounds, but nothing seems to be working for long.

So, this one particular idea has been in my head for a few years already, but I never haven't had enough time, or interest to make it happen.
So, this campaign mode. The gameplay wouldn't be changed too much. You could still play as long as you wanted, BUT with a little twist. Once you've gotten to round X, a door would open. Or any other kind of transition thing (train, car, plane.. Hole?) in which you could enter, and you would then go to another area of the map. So, let's say you're in Abandoned Hospital. The door opens, and you go in there. Boom, you're now in another section, as big as the first one, of the hospital.

Each level would have 3-5 sections in total, and once you've finished them all, you win. Yes, sounds weird? Winning in ZKW? Well, yes. You would win, survive another day. But you could still just stay, in any of these sections, and make your last stand, just like now.

So, any ideas? What does this make you feel?

So, this campaign mode. The gameplay wouldn't be changed too much. You could still play as long as you wanted, BUT with a little twist. Once you've gotten to round X, a door would open. Or any other kind of transition thing (train, car, plane.. Hole?) in which you could enter, and you would then go to another area of the map. So, let's say you're in Abandoned Hospital. So, any ideas? What does this make you feel?

[h1]So, you still care, eh?[/h1]
Ofcourse I care! Don't even ask something like that. Geez.
Anyways, as you know, it's been a long time since the previous "proper" update, and now I'm here to fix that.

True.. True.. Well, not really.
I just lost my motivation entirely for some reason. But now I'm getting it back! If everything goes well, you will be getting a new, proper, update for ZKW next weeks Friday! (22.4.2016)

[h1]So, what's in this, "proper", update then?[/h1]
Actually, I'm not yet sure about it all. I have so many ideas I want to make. But! One thing is for sure atleast.
You will be getting fancy..ed new player-menu (well, I just made it more fancy, that's all) and..

[h1]OverKill[/h1]
[img]http://files.1337upload.net/firepower-a081c8.png[/img]
Overkill is something that's really made for veteran ZKW players. Once you level up to Level 40, you will be given a option to reset your profile (well, only your level, really) and by doing so, you can select one of these OverKill "Perks". Currently, there are 6 of them, but I might be adding even more. I'm not going into details of what these special perks are just yet, but let me tell you.. They can change the gameplay very dramatically.
Also note, that it's not a must for someone to reset their profile. You can play to level 100 if you like. But if you do, you will actually be able to choose 2 OverKill perks! Let me explain.
When a player chooses to reset their profile for an OverKill perk at Level50, their profile will be resetted only to Level10. So, choosing an OverKill perk makes you go back 40 levels. Which means, that all those veteran players with Level80, or more, havent actually done it all for nothing!
I'll also note you, that it is possible to achieve every OverKill perk there is, as they are infinite. Once obtained, it will stay on forever (unless you choose to start a whole new game, that is) There still are couple OverKill perks, that only work once, and you can't select them anymore after it's been used.

I really hope this makes any sense to you, but if not, don't worry. You'll see what's up next week!

Keep slaying, and I keep developing!

One thing that's also taking my time nowadays, is a new project. Yes, I'm working on something else than ZKW (for the first time in almost 6 years!) and I'm having a blast with it :)

notes.title: Profile was corrupted after 1.1.8?
notes.content:
[b]If you were one of the unlucky ones, you should read this as there's still a chance we can save your profile. [/b]

[h1]Why did this happen?[/h1]
While the old version gave the user an fatal error, ending the game and preventing the corrupted profile from going anywhere, the 1.1.8 version chooses to ignore the fact that the profile was corrupted. Why? This was meant to fix the fatal error by just giving the user a more friendly message that the profile wasn't loaded correctly. For this reason, the game will actually continue to upload the (now corrupted) profile to ZKW's cloud, which then corrupted that as well.

[h1]So, what now?[/h1]
This bug has now been fixed, and patch is on it's way to Steam right now. [b]After updating[/b] to the new version, you need to [b]logout[/b] from your (possibly) corrupted profile, and [b]write your username[/b] here. I'll see if there's an [b]existing backup file of your profile, and restore that[/b] for you. 
[b]In case I can't find the backup[/b] file of your profile, I would like to give you [b]free ZKW-Points as an apologies.[/b]

notes.title: How do I use the Workshop?
notes.content:
[h1]Uploading your creations[/h1]
First of all, you need to make your level (in the level editor) After the level has been made, go to the [b]"FILE"[/b] tab on the top, and hit [b]"Share Map"[/b]
As easy as that!

[h1]Downloading others creations[/h1]
To download custom levels, go to Steam's Workshop. Find a level you would like to download, and hit the [b]"subscribe"[/b] button. After this, launch your ZKW-Reborn, and Steam will automatically load the level for you! You should then get a notification from ZKW that it has downloaded the map successfully. If not, just try to relaunch your ZKW, or Steam!
Remember to [b]run Steam as Adminstrator[/b] (and ZKW) if you're having any problems.

[h1]How to update existing map?[/h1]
At this point, you can't. It is recommended to upload your map with a slightly different name (for example. "My Map Version 2") and delete your old map (if you wish to do so)
